newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO firm on higher swaps and crude.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO firm on higher swaps and crude.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were expected to end firmer on Thursday on higher swaps and stronger crude values, traders said.
Traders said physical buyers are likely to bid at around $119 per tonne for 180 cst, up about one dollar from Wednesday.
The higher price came despite a rise in exports to the region from Kuwait and Venezuala, traders said.
Four 380-cst cargoes are arriving in Singapore later this month from Kuwait and these were sold at $1.50-2.40 a tonne above Singapore spot quotes on a cost-and-freight basis.
Singapore swaps are firmer with trades done Thursday for October at $118.75, $119.00 and $119.25, up from Wednesday's close of $117.25-118.00, brokers said.
"There is a possibility that prices would breach the previous high of $123.50 per tonne but I don't think it would be sustained," one trader said.
He said regional demand is not strong enough to keep prices at such high levels.
"The arrival of the cargoes in October and November would keep prices from rising further," he said.
Another trader said fuel oil prices are low relative to gas oil and this could lead to a reduction in fuel oil production as refiners optimise gas oil production.
